text:
pat: Quick report 00: noticed internal links to anchors with encoded characters failing after the doc build. Example: /reference/clients#c%2B%2B-usage doesn't scroll.

ana: Repro'd. The built id is `c-plus-plus-usage` so old `%2B` links break.

pat: I can patch the three highest-traffic pages with explicit header ids (e.g. `### C++ usage {#c-plus-plus-usage}`) so user-facing links stay stable.

own: Can we also add a tiny client-side fallback that normalizes hashes? Might avoid a larger sweep.

pat: Prototype I tried: `const s = decodeURIComponent(location.hash||'').replace(/\+/g,'plus').replace(/[^a-z0-9-]/gi,'-').toLowerCase(); if (document.getElementById(s)) location.replace('#'+s);` Simple and reversible.

ana: Fine as a short-term fix but add tests so linkcheck fails on internal anchor mismatches. Otherwise we'll miss regressions.

core-bot: CI: opened preview for pat's PR 4477 00: linkcheck queued.

core-bot: Linkcheck result: 2 warnings (external), 0 failures. Preview: https://deploy-preview-4477--docs.redwood.ai/reference/clients

own: Pat, please add a small note to migration guide describing how special characters map (+: plus, spaces->-, parens removed) so contributors know what changed.

pat: Done. PR merged. If anyone finds more odd anchors drop them here and I'll tag you on a follow-up sweep. :rocket:
